newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.EUROPE RAPESEED SET TO EASE AMID CROP PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: N.EUROPE RAPESEED SET TO EASE AMID CROP PRESSURE.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe are steady at 440 marks/tonne free Hamburg buyers but prices are expected to fall as the harvest gathers momentum, brokers said on Friday.
The market so far had been boosted by a firmer dollar.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were up on the week at 430-446 marks (425-437.50) for August.
But price falls in the Chicago soya complex on bearish weather news contributed to the emerging weaker sentiment here.
Yields and oil content from domestic harvests are meanwhile well above last year and the combined winter and spring rape area of 916,013 hectares exceeds 1996's 853,625 ha.
Harvesting was 80 percent complete in Germany's north where yields exceeded 4.00 tonnes per hectare (tph) compared with a national average 2.28 tph last year.
November rapeseed on the Matif futures traded at 459 marks, down one from Thursday's close and up two on the week.
In the products, rape meal gained up to 1.75 marks on the week on dollar-induced soymeal rises although rape meal is hard to market due to competition from imported mid-proteins.
Aug rape meal was at 23.50 marks/100 kg with Sept/Oct at 24.50 and Nov/Jan at 26.50.
Nearby rape oil prices were higher because supplies of competing soy oil were thinning in Rotterdam and in export markets.
Aug rape oil was up 0.25 on the week at 95.25 marks while Sept/Oct oil was down one mark at the same level.
